hunks.baseline: I almost failed to recognize him. That was how different Unnamed was from the person I had met a year ago. His face, speech, and atmosphere had all changed. Everything surrounding him felt unfamiliar and strange.
hunks.sol: I almost didn’t recognize him. Unnamed had changed that much since I’d met him a year ago. His face, his manner of speaking, the air about him—everything felt unfamiliar.

hunks.baseline: And the reason he had changed was probably…
hunks.sol: And the reason he’d changed was probably…

hunks.baseline: *It must be because of what happened that day, three months ago.*
hunks.sol: *What happened that day, three months ago.*

hunks.baseline: What was I supposed to say? My mouth felt bitter. I only spoke after Jung Ho and Hyuk Mujin left the room with the others.
hunks.sol: What was I supposed to say? I had a bitter taste in my mouth. I waited until Jung Ho and Hyuk Mujin had taken the others out of the room before I spoke.

hunks.baseline: “I haven’t been doing all that well, either. A lot more happened than I expected.”
hunks.sol: “I haven’t been doing all that well myself. More has happened than I expected.”

hunks.baseline: “It seems so. In fact, this humble monk only managed to hear about you two days ago.”
hunks.sol: “So it seems. In fact, I only learned what had happened to you two days ago.”

hunks.baseline: No martial artist could have remained unaware of the events that had unfolded over the past three months. But if Unnamed, who held an important position within Shaolin, had only heard about them two days ago, there was only one reason I could think of.
hunks.sol: No martial artist could have missed the events of the past three months. If Unnamed, who held an important position at Shaolin, had heard about them only two days ago, I could think of just one reason.

hunks.baseline: “You underwent closed-door training.”
hunks.sol: “You were in closed-door training.”

hunks.baseline: “Repentance Cave? Could it be…”
hunks.sol: “Repentance Cave? Does that mean…”

hunks.baseline: “You are correct. It was something I requested myself, so there is no need for you to worry.”
hunks.sol: “What you’re thinking is correct. I asked to go there myself, so please don’t worry.”

hunks.baseline: The first character meant shame; the second, remorse. Repentance Cave was where criminals were confined.
hunks.sol: The first character meant shame; the second, remorse. Repentance Cave was a place where sinners were confined.

hunks.baseline: What had he been so ashamed of? What did he need to repent for? Perhaps he regretted failing to prevent his Master from entering Nirvana. Unnamed had spent three months there, considering himself a sinner because he had failed to protect even the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the sacred treasure of Shaolin that his Master had entrusted to him before passing away.
hunks.sol: What was he ashamed of? What did he feel he had to repent for? Perhaps it was his regret at failing to prevent his Master’s death. Unnamed had spent three months there, calling himself a sinner for failing to protect even the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the divine artifact of Shaolin his Master had entrusted to him before he died.

hunks.baseline: “I had many thoughts in that darkness, where I could not see even an inch ahead.”
hunks.sol: “In the darkness, where I couldn’t see an inch in front of me, I kept thinking.”

hunks.baseline: Unnamed stroked his cheek with a callused finger. A large portion of his face, covered in scars both large and small, had turned dark bluish-black.
hunks.sol: Unnamed ran a callused finger over his cheek. Much of his scar-covered face had turned a dark bluish-black.

hunks.baseline: Three months ago, the Yin-Cold Qi left behind by the enemy he had risked his life to stop had left that mark. It was also a yoke he would never be free of.
hunks.sol: It was the mark left by the Yin-Cold Qi of the enemy he had risked his life to stop three months ago. A burden he would never be free of.

hunks.baseline: “I kept thinking that if only I had been a little stronger, I could have protected my Master. I could have properly carried out his final request.”
hunks.sol: “If only I’d been a little stronger, I might have protected my Master. I might have carried out his final request.”

hunks.baseline: But regret was always late. A venerable monk respected by everyone had entered Nirvana unexpectedly. Someone had lost a close friend. And someone else had been consumed by guilt over failing to fulfill even his Master’s final words, so he had entered Repentance Cave.
hunks.sol: But regret always came too late. A venerable monk respected by all had died unexpectedly. Someone had lost a close friend. And someone else, consumed by guilt at failing to carry out his Master’s final wishes, had gone into Repentance Cave.

hunks.baseline: *Anyone else would have been the same.*
hunks.sol: *Anyone would have felt the same.*

hunks.baseline: I would have been no different. I did not even want to imagine how I would have felt if I had failed to treat Jeok Cheongang and had been forced to watch him leave this world. I might have returned to the days when I was F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung and repeated the same cycle of deep regret and despair.
hunks.sol: I was no different. I didn’t even want to imagine how I would have felt if I’d failed to save Jeok Cheongang and had to let him go. Maybe I would have gone back to being F-rank Hunter Jin Taekyung, trapped in that same cycle of regret and despair.

hunks.baseline: But pain changes people. For better or worse. In Unnamed’s case, it had been for the better. His heart might have been broken, but at least in terms of advancing his martial arts, the pain had helped him.
hunks.sol: But pain changes people, for better or worse. In Unnamed’s case, it had changed him for the better. His heart might have been broken, but at least his martial arts had grown stronger.

hunks.baseline: “This is only my personal opinion, but I doubt you spent all your time thinking in Repentance Cave.”
hunks.sol: “This is just my opinion, but I doubt you spent all your time in Repentance Cave thinking.”

hunks.baseline: “Amitabha. Everything was thanks to the Buddha’s and Shaolin’s benevolence.”
hunks.sol: “Amitabha. I owe it all to the grace of the Buddha and Shaolin.”

hunks.baseline: Unnamed pressed his palms together toward the window, where sunlight streamed in, then gazed at me with calm eyes. There was a pure power in that gaze. A year ago, his body had been built from sturdy muscle. Now it had withered like an old tree. But the quiet aura flowing from his entire body was incomparable to what it had been before.
hunks.sol: Unnamed pressed his palms together toward the sunlit window, then looked at me with calm eyes. There was a pure power in his gaze. A year ago, his body had been packed with solid muscle. Now he was as lean as an old tree. But the quiet aura flowing from him was on another level from before.

hunks.baseline: *He crossed the wall.*
hunks.sol: *He’s broken through.*

hunks.baseline: The supreme realm every martial artist in Murim dreamed of reaching. There was no doubt that Unnamed had finally stepped into it.
hunks.sol: He had entered the supreme realm every martial artist dreamed of reaching. There was no doubt about it.

hunks.baseline: At the awed look in my eyes, Unnamed gave a small nod.
hunks.sol: Seeing the awe in my eyes, Unnamed gave a small nod.

hunks.baseline: “To heal a body that had fallen into critical condition and advance to a higher realm, I needed more than enlightenment. The Great Restoration Pill was one of those things.”
hunks.sol: “Enlightenment alone wasn’t enough to heal a body in critical condition and reach a higher realm. I needed many other things. The Great Restoration Pill was one of them.”

hunks.baseline: If it was Shaolin’s Great Restoration Pill, it was an elixir whose effects ranked among the very best in the world.
hunks.sol: Shaolin’s Great Restoration Pill was among the finest elixirs in the world.

hunks.baseline: *Yes. If it was the Great Restoration Pill, it might have been possible.*
hunks.sol: *Right. With the Great Restoration Pill, it might have been possible.*

hunks.baseline: The pill’s effects were one thing, but Unnamed was the Disciple whom Dharma King Hong Dao, a man capable of reading heavenly patterns, had personally brought in and raised with all his heart. He was a genius born with tremendous martial talent—not quite on Cheongpung’s level, perhaps, but still extraordinary. There was no doubt that he was worthy of the Great Restoration Pill.
hunks.sol: The pill was extraordinary, but so was Unnamed. Dharma King Hong Dao, who could read the heavenly patterns, had brought him to Shaolin himself and poured his heart into raising him. Unnamed was a genius with tremendous martial talent—not quite on Cheongpung’s level, perhaps, but surely worthy of the Great Restoration Pill.

hunks.baseline: He had reached the Supreme Peak realm while still in his thirties, proving not only his Master’s discerning eye, but also his own talent.
hunks.sol: He had reached the Supreme Peak realm while still in his thirties. That proved both his Master’s eye for talent and his own ability.

hunks.baseline: “Congratulations. I heard the Great Restoration Pill is an extremely precious item even within Shaolin.”
hunks.sol: “Congratulations. I’ve heard the Great Restoration Pill is precious even by Shaolin’s standards.”

hunks.baseline: “That is why this humble monk vehemently refused it. But my Senior Brother Abbot gave it to me, telling me not to ask any questions. As it turned out, my Master seems to have said something about it several years ago. Perhaps… he knew this would happen.”
hunks.sol: “That’s why I refused it so firmly. But my Senior Brother, the Abbot, gave it to me and told me not to ask questions. Apparently, my Master had said something to him about it several years ago. Perhaps… he knew this would happen.”

hunks.baseline: A faint smile touched Unnamed’s lips. He gazed into empty space for a moment, as though remembering his Master, then continued.
hunks.sol: A faint smile touched Unnamed’s lips. He gazed into the distance for a moment, as though remembering his Master, then went on.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, my Senior Brother Abbot would also like to meet Benefactor Jin.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, the Abbot would like to meet you too, Benefactor Jin.”

hunks.baseline: “Your Senior Brother Abbot?”
hunks.sol: “The Abbot?”

hunks.baseline: I had never heard anything about the next Abbot after Dharma King Hong Dao. According to Gung Gibang, it was supposed to be one of the Dharma King’s direct Disciples, but spectacular events had kept occurring one after another, and I had never found the time to think about it.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t heard who had succeeded Dharma King Hong Dao. Gung Gibang had said it would be one of the Dharma King’s direct Disciples, but one spectacular disaster after another had kept me too busy to think about it.

hunks.baseline: “The two of you have probably never met face-to-face. In our lineage, he is my eldest Senior Brother, but he has been Abbot for less than a month, so it is only natural that you would not know him.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t believe you’ve met him. He’s my eldest Senior Brother in our lineage, and he became Abbot less than a month ago. It’s only natural that you wouldn’t know him.”

hunks.baseline: “He said that he was sorry he had been too distracted to even say goodbye before sending you away last time.”
hunks.sol: “He said he was sorry things had been so chaotic last time that he let you leave without even saying goodbye.”

hunks.baseline: “He doesn’t need to apologize. I was in such a daze back then that I could hardly think straight, either.”
hunks.sol: “He doesn’t need to apologize. I was barely thinking straight myself.”

hunks.baseline: The Shaolin Bloodshed that had occurred during the Star-Array Grand Banquet had been an unprecedented incident, but I had left Henan for Sichuan within a day or two. To save Jeok Cheongang, who was in critical condition, I had needed to find the Divine Physician as quickly as possible.
hunks.sol: The Shaolin Bloodshed during the Star-Array Grand Banquet had been unprecedented, but I’d had to leave Henan for Sichuan within a day or two. Jeok Cheongang was in critical condition, and finding the Divine Physician couldn’t wait.

hunks.baseline: “Amitabha. This humble monk was truly delighted when he belatedly heard that Benefactor Jeok had made a full recovery. My Master, who must be watching over me from somewhere, would have been relieved to see his friend in good health.”
hunks.sol: “Amitabha. I was truly glad when I finally heard that Benefactor Jeok had made a full recovery. My Master must be watching over me from somewhere. I’m sure he was relieved to see his friend well again.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, now that you mention it, you must have already met Old— No, my Master.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, speaking of which, you must have met the Old— No, my Master already.”

hunks.baseline: “Until you woke up, we had been speaking together. At first, I almost failed to recognize him.”
hunks.sol: “We spoke until you woke up. I nearly failed to recognize him at first.”

hunks.baseline: “Well, he, uh… did change a little.”
hunks.sol: “Well, he has, uh… changed a little.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. He changed as much as this humble monk did.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. About as much as I have.”

hunks.baseline: As I hesitated in response to the sudden self-deprecating joke, Unnamed politely pressed his palms together.
hunks.sol: While I hesitated over his sudden self-deprecating joke, Unnamed politely pressed his palms together.

hunks.baseline: “Amitabha. It was a joke.”
hunks.sol: “Amitabha. That was a joke.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh. Ah. I see.”
hunks.sol: “Oh. Ah. Right.”

hunks.baseline: “You do not seem to have found it amusing. This humble monk will refrain from doing so again.”
hunks.sol: “You didn’t find it amusing. I’ll refrain from making another.”

hunks.baseline: The words *Please do* rose all the way to my throat.
hunks.sol: *Please do* rose to the tip of my tongue.

hunks.baseline: A joke like that was only funny when it came from someone who hadn’t suffered quite so much. When Unnamed said it, the mood could only turn solemn in an instant. But I did not have the courage to nod.
hunks.sol: A joke like that was funny coming from someone who hadn’t suffered quite so much. Coming from Unnamed, it made the whole room turn solemn. But I didn’t have the courage to nod.

hunks.baseline: “…No. It was funny.”
hunks.sol: “…No, it was funny.”

hunks.baseline: “Amitabha. Then this humble monk will continue.”
hunks.sol: “Amitabha. Then I’ll continue.”

hunks.baseline: “That was the end of the joke.”
hunks.sol: “That was the joke.”

hunks.baseline: I stared at Unnamed in disbelief, then let out a quiet laugh. Still, the fact that he was making such clumsy jokes meant he had weathered everything much better than I had expected.
hunks.sol: I stared at him, dumbfounded, then let out a quiet laugh. If he could make clumsy jokes like these, he’d come through it better than I’d feared.

hunks.baseline: Even if I could not offer him any comfort, I could at least listen to his borderline temple jokes.
hunks.sol: I might not be able to comfort him, but I could at least listen to a few temple jokes that pushed the limits.

hunks.baseline: *That aside…*
hunks.sol: *Anyway…*

hunks.baseline: The sun was shining outside the window, so I seemed to have slept for a full day. But I had no idea where we actually were. As I looked around the room once more, Unnamed explained.
hunks.sol: Judging by the sun outside, I’d slept for about a full day, but I still had no idea where we were. I looked around again, and Unnamed explained.

hunks.baseline: “We are at an inn near Mount Song. It was rented in the name of the Murim Alliance, so please stay here and get plenty of rest.”
hunks.sol: “An inn near Mount Song. It’s been rented in the name of the Murim Alliance, so please stay and rest as long as you need.”

hunks.baseline: It had been a distant-sounding term, but hearing it directly from Unnamed in Henan made it feel much more real. I got out of bed and approached the window to look at the scenery outside.
hunks.sol: The name had always felt distant. Hearing Unnamed say it here in Henan made it suddenly real. I got out of bed and went to the window.

hunks.baseline: The first thing that caught my eye was the peak of Mount Song, rising in the distance so high it seemed to pierce the sky. Beneath it, buildings were packed densely along the mountain’s lower slopes, and people of every kind filled my view.
hunks.sol: The first thing I saw was a peak of Mount Song rising in the distance as though it might pierce the sky. Buildings crowded the foot of the mountain, and all sorts of people filled the streets.

hunks.baseline: A Murim practitioner with a narrow-bladed sword at his waist. Another carrying a massive saber on his back without even a scabbard. Others carrying spears and twin axes…
hunks.sol: One martial artist had a narrow-bladed sword at his waist. Another carried a massive saber on his back without a scabbard. Others bore spears and twin axes…

hunks.baseline: Yes, they were all different, but something felt wrong.
hunks.sol: All sorts of people, sure. But something was off.

hunks.baseline: At the sight of me watching the Murim practitioners everywhere I looked, Unnamed let out a low laugh.
hunks.sol: Unnamed gave a low laugh as I watched the martial artists everywhere I looked.

hunks.baseline: “Amitabha. They are Benefactors who heard the news and gathered from every corner of the world.”
hunks.sol: “Amitabha. They’ve come from all across the land after hearing the news.”

hunks.baseline: “Even a quick glance makes it seem like there are more of them than there were at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
hunks.sol: “Even at a glance, there seem to be more of them than there were at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

hunks.baseline: “If the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a festival for young prodigies, the founding of the Murim Alliance concerns everyone. Members of the orthodox and unorthodox factions have gathered, along with a considerable number of eccentric experts who were previously little known and had been living in seclusion.”
hunks.sol: “The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a festival for young prodigies. The founding of the Murim Alliance concerns everyone. People from both the orthodox and unorthodox factions are here, and quite a few little-known eccentrics have come out of seclusion as well.”

hunks.baseline: That made sense. The scale alone was entirely different, so it was only natural that so many people had gathered. If the Star-Array Grand Banquet had been the Han River fireworks festival, the founding of the Murim Alliance was Jindotgae One.[^1] Perhaps for that reason, there were almost no commoners to be seen, unlike during the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
hunks.sol: That made sense. The stakes were entirely different, so of course more people had come. If the Star-Array Grand Banquet was the Han River fireworks festival, the founding of the Murim Alliance was Jindotgae One.[^1] Unlike at the banquet, there were hardly any commoners in sight.

hunks.baseline: *They can feel it too. They must know what is happening here.*
hunks.sol: *They can feel it too. They know what’s happening here.*

hunks.baseline: As I thought that to myself, a group of Murim practitioners crossing the main road suddenly caught my eye. Their aura was unusual enough that they could not be mistaken for ordinary martial artists. They clearly belonged to one of the great prestigious factions.
hunks.sol: As I thought that, a group of martial artists crossing the main road caught my eye. Their qi was too remarkable for them to be ordinary fighters. They had to belong to a prestigious faction.

hunks.sol: I didn’t need to ask Unnamed. Wrapped in furs despite the warm spring day and wearing leather armor unlike the other martial artists, they drew whispers wherever they went.

hunks.baseline: “Could they be…”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. They’re the Murong Family.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. The Murong Family.”

hunks.baseline: “My word. It’s well over a thousand li from Liaoning to Henan. They arrived quickly.”
hunks.sol: “My word. It’s well over a thousand li from Liaoning to Henan. They got here quickly.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you think people call them descendants of horse-riding nomads for nothing? What luck. I never expected to see people from the Murong Family in my lifetime.”
hunks.sol: “They’re said to have the blood of horse-riding nomads for a reason. What luck. I never thought I’d see members of the Murong Family in my lifetime.”

hunks.baseline: It was my first time seeing the Murong Family, too. Shanxi Province, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was located, was also considered a frontier region, but Liaoning lay far to the northeast beyond Hebei. It was not somewhere one could visit as casually as the neighborhood next door.
hunks.sol: It was my first time seeing them too. Shanxi Province, home to the Jin Family of Taiyuan, counted as a frontier region, but Liaoning was a long way northeast, beyond Hebei. It wasn’t the sort of place you visited like the neighborhood next door.

hunks.baseline: They were so far away that I had heard even members of the Murong Family rarely ventured into the Central Plains.

hunks.baseline: *So this is that Murong Family.*
hunks.sol: *So that’s the Murong Family.*

hunks.baseline: As one of the stronger families among the Five Great Families, the Murong Family’s reputation had reached my ears so often that I was sick of hearing it. I had heard that, unlike other factions, they even operated a cavalry unit.

hunks.baseline: The moment that thought occurred to me as I looked at the people outside—

hunks.sol: A tremendous roar sounded from somewhere.
